960	I heard my father rule on this several times for people who find it hard to give maaser; some poskim write

961	that one may deduct all the expenses needed to maintain the household.

962	A person has a family: he has to pay rent, pay property tax, pay electricity, pay water, has to

963	pay boarding school for the children, certainly for the older children.

964	You are obligated to educate them, but boarding, food and clothing for older children, some say you are no longer obligated to give

965	them; they are grown, they are on their own, past bar mitzvah.

966	All the expenses surrounding the tuition itself, which is "and you shall teach them to your sons," apart from the tuition itself, some say

967	that in a case where a person is struggling, he may deduct them from the maaser.

968	So that is from the halachic standpoint.

969	But we need to know, and this is a very important point, maaser is not only an obligation, it is a privilege.

970	True, in terms of the obligation, one can, as we said, find all kinds of shortcuts, deduct here, expand

971	your expenses more and more and more, and say, nothing is left for me for maaser.

972	Because if I deduct all the expenses of the month, I have no income left, no profit left anymore.

973	That is true.

974	But along with that, as the Rebbe wrote many times, maaser is also a privilege, maaser is our way

975	to say to the Holy One, Blessed be He, believe in us.

976	To say to the Holy One, Blessed be He, bring us into Your partnership.

977	Put Your check in our bank account.

978	And therefore one must make an effort to give maaser.

979	Even if you have all kinds of legal ways in which you can reduce your maaser, we still need to remember

980	that maaser is a great mitzvah, and a great privilege, and it is worth giving it.

981	Therefore the Rav said that one should always try as much as possible to overcome the difficulties and give the maaser.

982	And in practice, there is one very special point that the Rebbe wrote in several letters, and with this we will finish: in a case where a person

983	is in great difficulty, who would usually give, but fell into hard times, and everyone has such times, even if he is

984	an employee, certainly if he is self-employed, suddenly there are hard times.

985	The Rebbe said, give as much as you can.

986	Once he wrote to give a maaser of the maaser.

987	To give one percent.

988	And once he said to give as much as you can, and write the rest in a notebook, how much you owe

989	for maaser, and with the help of HaShem, when the Holy One, Blessed be He, allows it, you will repay.

990	That is, if you have hard times when you cannot give, do not give up on it.

991	Write on a note: I gave one percent, I gave two, I gave five percent; with the help of HaShem, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will enable me each

992	month to add how much you owe for maaser.

993	The very fact that you want to give, the very fact that you commit to give, certainly if it is about more than maaser, about fifteen

994	percent or a chomesh, the very fact that a person commits, that itself opens gates for him; the Holy One, Blessed be He, sees how much he wants

995	to give.

996	Consequently, the Holy One, Blessed be He, opens gates for him and repays him.

997	So we are finishing.

998	Maaser is our way of saying to the Holy One, Blessed be He: we appreciate Your help, we appreciate Your partnership,

999	give to us and we will know what to do with it.

1000	May we merit that the Holy One, Blessed be He, gives, and that we always be among the givers and not among the receivers.

1001	And most important, as the Gemara in Bava Batra says, great is tzedakah, for it brings the redemption near; what better reason is there

1002	to excel in the mitzvah of maasrot?

1003	Because when we open our hearts to others, the Holy One, Blessed be He, opens His heart to us and gives us salvation and deliverance

1004	and everything we ask for: a complete redemption.

1005	Right now, truly, on the eve of the month of Kislev, and for Chabad this is the month of redemption, the eve of Rosh Chodesh Kislev, may we merit, with the help of HaShem,
